the_ruling_verbatim: Code Mother isn't a builder. Aider turned out not to be a good enough builder. so we have one builder, you. so if something is waiting, it's not _nobody has taken it up_ as much as it is _cc has not had time yet_. a fleet of one so far. :)

So that being said: :waiting for 'waiting for somebody to do me' (as in TICKETME BUILDME etc) is fine. :inprocess as a state for 'i'm doing it now' is groovy. :queued <-- this is new, and means it's blocked by another ticket's completion. :hold <-- this is new, and this is the state for our 'cognition' tickets. they're on hold until the other work is done. :blocked <-- this is new, and means there's a problem and it can't move forward and you can't sort on your own what to do with it next.
nothing passes a gate with prose. an inspector will not allow it. not only has to have a field, but valid data to the limits of detection of deterministic code. we can add more sieves as needed.
Of course hold is a graveyard risk, but it's in the reports. it shows up. and it should show up in the operator inbox specifically so the operator is kept aware "you've got a hold on these".
in process should be AUTOMATICALLY cleared in post build part of the sail skill.
stateless read on in-process makes sense to me
exactly so. the source of truth is the picture in my head. everything else is working toward a more and more faithful implementation of that.
now_the_spec_says: The pickup phase answers why a ticket is not moving, not who holds it: waiting, in-process, queued, hold, blocked. in-process is DERIVED, never stored. Every written phase carries a deterministically-valid release field. hold and blocked are inbox.
context: THE FLEET IS ONE -- CC is the sole builder; CodeMother is not one and aider did not become one. So :waiting means 'CC has not had time', not 'nobody took it up', and the slot's axis moves from WHO HOLDS IT to WHY IT IS NOT MOVING. _PHASES grows two -> five: waiting (nobody on it yet), in-process (being done now), queued (blocked by another ticket's completion), hold (deliberately parked until other work finishes -- the cognition tickets today), blocked (a problem CC cannot sort alone). Sorted by who acts next: CC (waiting, in-process); nobody, it self-clears (queued); Akien (hold, blocked). That sort IS the inbox sieve, which the inbox cannot compute today. IN-PROCESS IS DERIVED because it is runtime state -- true only while a process runs -- and the ticket file is git-tracked and shared, so a committed :in-process claims a hand that is gone once the session ends and is false on any machine that pulls it. Nothing writes it; nothing clears it. EVERY WRITTEN PHASE CARRIES A FIELD, NOT PROSE, valid to the limits of deterministic detection: queued names the ticket it waits on (self-clearing, machine-checkable), blocked names the question or trouble that releases it, hold names the condition that ends it. HOLD IS AN INBOX ITEM, not reference -- the operator is kept aware 'you've got a hold on these', which is how the graveyard risk is paid for instead of avoided; blocked is inbox as an ESCALATION. -- MEASURED FIRST (2026-09-08, opened by Akien asking why every dashboard ticket reads :waiting): 51 of 258 tickets carry :waiting, 205 a bare pre-phase cursor, and ZERO have ever carried :in-process. The pickup door exists (transitions.py:1889) with 13 journaled records, all actor CC, all 2026-08-07..2026-08-10, and no caller anywhere in the live system. Probe cairn/tools/base/probes/a_pickup_is_witnessed.py clears on pickups >= 1, so it took its 1 in August and reads green forever off a historical fact. -- CC WAS CORRECTED TWICE: it proposed a staleness red for stranded :in-process (Akien replaced it with automatic post-build clearing, then with a stateless read, dissolving the problem instead of detecting it), and it sorted hold OUT of the inbox (overruled -- awareness is the point). -- WHY A RULING: it changes the transition grammar's vocabulary, narrows a standing ruling's premise, and moves an inbox sort. CC's read that the 2026-08-07 side-channel clause is SUPERSEDED BY THE REFRAME RATHER THAN VIOLATED was put to him explicitly and confirmed 'exactly so', with the principle restated: the source of truth is the picture in his head, every artifact a translation working toward it (Law 9). -- STILL OPEN, NOT RULED: whether queued -> in-process is legal directly or must pass back through waiting (CC's read: through waiting, so 'dependency cleared' and 'a hand is on it' stay two recorded acts). UNBUILT: _PHASES is still the two-tuple; nothing is cast. -- WHAT NARROWS RATHER THAN DIES (nothing is deleted, so what_dies is empty): 2026-08-07-the-ticket-is-the-source-period keeps its core -- the ticket is THE SOURCE PERIOD, the phase is cursor annotation, every summons inherits a pickup, terminals take none. What narrows is the multi-actor premise it was written against ('the tester picks up the ticket and all those different things have to know what to push'), because a fleet of one has no second picker-up. The pickup door's derived clause at transitions.py:1899 -- 'nobody derives "is anyone on this?" from a side channel' -- is superseded for the same reason: with one hand, the live session is the same hand, not a side channel. a_pickup_is_witnessed.py must stop clearing on a historical existence claim.
